extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and readers of medieval literature and literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and critical principles for judging and understanding medieval romance and chivalric poetry (Arthurian, Carolingian, Persian/Arabian influences, and German romances), with attention to purpose, form, national character, and imaginative qualities. Focuses on what makes these fictions valuable or defective in their historical and aesthetic contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: True end of poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The true end of poetry is to awaken or restore aspirations and feelings which are the poetry of nature; by setting all things in the most beautiful light and investing all things with loveliness and magic, not so much to ennoble or exalt our feelings, as to preserve and sustain them in their natural element of beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry's aim is restorative and aspirational — to revive natural poetic feelings through beauty and enchantment rather than through didactic moralizing. Use imagery and tone that preserve feeling rather than over-explain it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the marvellous and chivalrous clothing
rubrics_metrics.description: The poetical clothing of the marvellous and the chivalrous, under which the fate of love is represented, has the effect of at once beautifying the fiction, and ennobling the feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ marvelous, chivalric elements to beautify and elevate emotional content. These devices should enhance the fiction's emotional resonance (e.g., elegiac tenderness in Tristram or bright romance in Launcelot).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of excessive prosaic realism and microscopic psychology
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern poets, imprisoned as they are within a world of present and prosaic realities, endeavour to atone for the want of poetry by a display of natural and moral knowledge, and the wire-drawn minuteness of psychology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat this as an anti-pattern: excessive emphasis on contemporary prosaic detail and over-analytical psychology weakens poetic effect. Prefer suggestion, beauty, and imaginative shaping over forensic psychological description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance allegory with adventure (spiritual knighthood without sacrificing wonders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetical historians endeavoured, under the form of Arthur and his knights, to shadow forth the idea of a spiritual knighthood ... This idea, however, is not allowed to interfere with the external rules of their fiction, or to make them sacrifice any of those adventures and wonders of love and war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using allegory (e.g., spiritual knighthood, St. Graal), retain the external narrative attractions — adventures, wonders, and romance — so allegory deepens rather than replaces the story's chivalric spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transplantability / scope of mythic system
rubrics_metrics.description: The elder poetry of the Arabs ... is so very local, that, so far from being capable of being transplanted into other regions, in order to understand it perfectly, we ought to become profoundly versant in all the genealogies of the Arabs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works relying on extremely local genealogies, customs, or narrowly confined references risk limited transmission and comprehension; by contrast, mythological systems and universal heroic ideas travel more readily between cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of romantic fictions: historicity, nationality, imagination, and love
rubrics_metrics.description: Their value is always so much the higher in proportion as they are more dependent on a historical foundation, more national in their import and character, and more abounding in a free, natural, and unaffected display of imagination,—above all, in proportion as they are imbued with the spirit of love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these four axes when assessing romances: (1) rootedness in history/tradition, (2) expression of national character, (3) freedom and naturalness of imaginative display, (4) presence of the spirit of love. Stronger works score higher on these combined qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: National feeling combined with heroic grandeur and sentimental tenderness
rubrics_metrics.description: The best chivalrous poem ... should express so much national feeling, and give to its marvellous so much of the character of power and greatness as might entitle it to be considered as a heroic poem, while ... it should preserve in the department of feeling all that beauty, and tenderness, and love, which formed the excellence of the sentimental poetry of the Troubadours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a synthesis: heroic scope and grandeur (power of the marvelous) plus the intimate beauty and tenderness of love-poetry. Excess toward one pole (pure epic or pure sentimentality) is viewed as a defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spirit of love as moral/aesthetic temper in tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a tragical catastrophe is ... introduced ... [it] never allows us to close with the single feeling of destruction, oppression, or an inevitable fate — which bids the victim of sorrows and death rise to a higher life ... and offers ... the sure prospect of a recompense for all his endurance — a crown of victory in the heavens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in tragic outcomes, chivalric/Christian romances should elevate the sufferer toward transcendent consolation or moral recompense; despair as an end-state is artistically unsatisfying in this tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal design for oral performance and structural regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: It has an almost dramatic conclusion, and is divided into six books: these again are subdivided into smaller sections, cantos, or rhapsodies, with a view, it is probable, to oral recitation or singing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing or evaluating medieval-style romances, consider structural regularity (books, cantos, rhapsodies) that suit oral performance: clear divisions, memorable conclusions, and modular episodes help transmission and recitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melodic versification and softness of feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Several German romances ... in their unbroken melody of versification and softness of feeling, are entirely similar to the old poetry of Provence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smooth, musical versification and a soft sentimental tone are virtues in love-romances; rhythmic continuity and melodic quality enhance the emotional effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegorical depth and learned erudition (with risk of pedantry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wolkram Von Eschenbach ... has seized ... the idea of that doubly allegorical method of treating them ... he bears no small resemblance to Dante ... in his propensity to allegories, and in his love of displaying, with some little pedantry, his extensive erudition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep allegory and learned allusion can enrich a romance (e.g., double allegory of spiritual and temporal meanings), but authors should avoid letting erudition become merely pedantic display that distracts from poetic power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use setting distance to expand imaginative freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: The poets were ... more partial to the fabulous histories of Charlemagne and Arthur, because they were well aware that the more distant their scene was laid, the more room had they for the exercise of their fancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing action in distant or antiquated settings increases imaginative liberty and acceptance of marvels; use historical or far-off settings to justify and enable fantastical elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eastern influence as ornamental brilliancy, not foundational replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: All that the western poetry owed to that of the east, with regard to these particulars, consisted in a certain southern magic, and oriental brilliancy of fancy, with which these familiar forms came about this time to be invested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borrowed oriental motifs should act as ornamental enhancement (magic, brilliance) to native forms rather than wholly supplanting indigenous character. Acknowledge influence but preserve core national spirit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate works in their own historical and cultural context
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who are perpetually tracing resemblances between the poets of different countries and ages ... are in general either insignificant or imaginary, for every true poet is a being by himself. If we must compare the poems of that age to something, let it be, not to the poems of other times, but to the other works of art which were produced in their own time, and in their own country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should prioritize contemporaneous and local artistic standards (architecture, social forms) rather than forced cross-era likenesses. Judge works relative to their own cultural moment.
